nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the cofactor threshold $h(n)$ is the largest natural number $m$ such that for every set $A$ of exactly $n$ positive integers, the set $\{a/\gcd(a,b) : a, b \in A\}$ has at least $m$ elements.
nodes.title: Erdős cofactor threshold

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $h(n)$ be the largest natural number $m$ such that for every set $A$ of exactly $n$ positive integers, the set $\{a/\gcd(a,b) : a, b \in A\}$ has at least $m$ elements. Then $\sqrt{n} = O(h(n))$ as $n \to \infty$: there are a real constant $C$ and an $n_0$ such that $\sqrt{n} \le C\,h(n)$ for all natural numbers $n \ge n_0$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 539: square-root lower bound for the cofactor threshold

nodes.summary: Let $h(n)$ denote the cofactor threshold of $n$. The statement is that $\sqrt{n} = O(h(n))$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, there are a real constant $C$ and an $n_0$ such that $\sqrt{n} \le C\,h(n)$ for all natural numbers $n \ge n_0$.
nodes.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 539

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, $m$ is a cofactor lower bound for $n$ when, for every set $A$ of exactly $n$ positive integers, the set $\{a/\gcd(a,b) : a, b \in A\}$ has at least $m$ elements.
